source.title: A finite sample analysis of the benign overfitting phenomenon for ridge function estimation

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a finite-sample theoretical analysis of prediction for minimum-norm interpolators in a nonlinear ridge-function model, rather than reproducing the original empirical sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds, not measured test-error curves. The explicit statement that a bound worsens as n/p approaches 1 is included in the prediction-bound row; cited results from other papers and estimation-distance bounds are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a purely theoretical paper. It gives only upper bounds on estimation distance and prediction error for minimum-norm interpolators in a ridge-function model, and only for the overparameterized regime. There is no lower bound, no realized or exact risk, and no underparameterized prediction bound to compare against. A worsening upper bound near n/p→1 (Remark 3.2) and a shrinking bound as p→∞ cannot show that risk actually peaks, rises with n, or descends a second time. The paper frames its results within double descent and benign overfitting, but its results cannot confirm or refute any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors present a finite-sample analysis of benign overfitting for linear and some nonlinear ridge-function models, giving estimation-distance and high-probability prediction bounds for the minimum-norm interpolator in the overparameterized regime. They say the bound worsening as n/p→1 is in accordance with double descent. They name deep networks, penalization and weaker assumptions as future work.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical finite-sample analysis of minimum-norm ERM for ridge-function models, rather than the original empirical model-size, epoch, and sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that its prediction bound worsens as n/p approaches 1 from below. Remark 3.2 illustrates this for isotropic data; the theorem also allows general A under its assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: For the minimum-norm interpolator in a single-index or ridge-function model with subGaussian random design, the high-probability prediction-error upper bound (Thm 3.1) has a term ~√n/(√((1−α)p)−C√n). This term blows up as n approaches p from below and shrinks as p grows (Remark 3.2; Sec. 2.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-sample upper bounds on prediction error for minimum-norm interpolators in nonlinear ridge-function models degrade near n≈p and improve as p/n grows. This is consistent with benign overfitting, but is a bound rather than a demonstrated risk curve.

record.problems: The evidence on the claimed curve is theoretical and bound-based; no realized test-error curve or direct sample-size sweep is reported. The results depend on the paper's stated random-design and regularity assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: Estimation-distance results in Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 and Corollaries 2.4 and 2.5 are excluded because they measure distance to the true parameter rather than the prediction-error behavior named by the claim.

untested.parts: No realized or exact risk as a function of n. Only an upper bound that worsens as n/p→1 is given.
No risk curve across capacity on both sides of the interpolation threshold. Only overparameterized upper bounds are given.
No label-noise, multiple-peak or regularization analysis. Penalization is listed only as future work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its limits_scope labels are overturned. An upper bound alone cannot establish or qualify an effect on risk, so no verdicts are given. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: No deep-network model-size sweep or test-error curve.
The paper discusses how its prediction-error upper bound changes as n/p approaches 1; it does not report realized test errors under changes in sample size.

The analysis concerns an overparameterized ridge-function model and a prediction-error bound; it does not report a full risk curve across model classes or compare both sides of the interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.
No study of peak dependence on label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective parameter measure or demonstration that a second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: minimum ℓ2-norm interpolating ERM in the ridge function model with random design
rows.operation_detail: Derived a finite-sample prediction-error bound for the minimum-norm interpolating solution in the overparameterized regime; the authors note how the bound changes as n/p changes.

conditions.value: random design; independent subGaussian vectors, with the stated model assumptions
general A in the theorem; isotropic data A = I in Remark 3.2

rows.measure: Theoretical upper bound on prediction error for a new data point; not a measured test error.
rows.value: Theorem 3.1 gives a bound involving |εₙ₊₁|, t KZ ||A⊤θ*||₂, (n/p) log(n/τ), and a term proportional to √n/(√((1−α)p) − CKZ√n). Remark 3.2 states that for isotropic data the upper bound worsens as n grows while n remains below p and n/p approaches 1.
rows.uncertainty: Theorem 3.1 gives a probability guarantee; it is at least 1 minus the stated exponential terms.
rows.note: This is a bound on prediction error, not evidence that realized test error rises with sample size or falls as capacity grows. The paper does not provide a full double-descent curve.
rows.check: The row reports an upper bound on prediction error, not a measured or exact risk. An upper bound worsening as n/p→1 cannot show that test error rises with n (V3). The bound covers only the overparameterized side, so it cannot show a peak or a second descent (V4). The baseline is correctly not stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
